title: Orchid Labs — token economics and latency scan
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
summary: Discovery call to map Orchid Labs' latency & throughput targets and decide between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private. Customer wants p95 sub-400ms for short chat flows, supports bursty token storms up to 3k concurrent requests, interested in streaming responses, kiosk of security requirements (SSO/SAML, SOC2, KMS). Agreed to run a token/sec benchmark harness and share traffic patterns; Redwood to send pricing and benchmark plan.
next_steps: Redwood: send Hosted vs Dedicated cost comparison and example SLOs (Maya) by 2026-04-15
Redwood SE: deliver benchmark harness plan + sample scripts (Jonah) by 2026-04-16
Customer: upload traffic histogram (token lengths, qps, tail spikes) to shared drive (Priya) by 2026-04-14
Schedule 60-min pilot kickoff to run token/sec and streaming trials week of 2026-04-20
action_items: Maya Patel: Send pricing and Dedicated vs Hosted cost comparison by 2026-04-15
Jonah Reed: Prepare token/sec benchmark harness and sample workload (incl. streaming, prefix caching) by 2026-04-16

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-12 09:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Priya (Orchid CTO), Marcus (Lead ML Eng), Samir (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): map p95 targets, concurrency profile, decide whether Hosted can meet p95 w/ caching or if Dedicated/Private is needed for sustained throughput.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for making time. i'm maya, i'm the AE on this account. quick intros?
[00:05] Priya (Orchid): hey i'm priya, cto at orchid. we build realtime support and analysis tools for clinical workflows. marcus and samir are on from infra and ml.
[00:12] Marcus (Orchid): yep, hi.
[00:13] Samir (Orchid): hi all.
[00:15] Jonah (Redwood SE): hey team, jonah here, i'll be the technical lead for the benchmark work, glad to dig in.
[00:20] Maya: quick agenda: map your latency p95 targets, peak concurrency/bursts, streaming behavior, and security constraints so we can propose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. any other items?
[00:29] Priya: nope that's it. we mostly want to know if hosted with caching and batching can hit our p95 and cost targets, or if we need dedicated hardware. plus compliance notes.
[00:35] Jonah: cool. Priya, can you give us concrete numbers for your p95 and concurrency?
[00:40] Priya: sure. for our short chat flows (20-120 tokens) we target p95 under 400ms end-to-end — that's from user keystroke to token render in-stream. for longer summarization jobs (1k-2k tokens) we tolerate up to 2s p95 but prefer lower.
[00:55] Maya: good, and concurrency?
[00:58] Priya: baseline ~150 concurrent active sessions, but we get bursts — product launches or overnight ingestion — that can hit 2.5k concurrent requests for a few minutes. bursts are highly spiky; 95% of the time we run under 300 concurrency.
[01:14] Jonah: okay that's helpful. do you stream tokens to clients in the short flows?
[01:18] Marcus: yes, streaming is essential for UX. we also have a small percentage of non-streaming batch jobs for nightly summarization.
[01:25] Jonah: got it. so streaming p95 for short flows is a big driver. what model family are you planning to use?
[01:30] Priya: we're testing an open LlaMa-variant and a 70B family. we also looked at some smaller 13B distils for cost. model selection may change but the patterns are similar.
[01:39] Maya: one clarifying Q on SLO scope — when you say p95 under 400ms is that client-side plus network, or strictly server-side inference?
[01:46] Priya: that's end-to-end, so we'd like the server-side part in the 200-300ms p95 ideally so we can stay under 400ms after network.
[01:55] Jonah: okay that translates to ~180-250ms p95 for server inference on a per-request short-stream path if we include prefix/caching benefits.
[02:03] Samir: our infra lives in GCP us-west, we have private networking and stricter egress rules. data residency isn't deep but we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, and KMS integration for keys.
[02:14] Maya: Redwood supports SSO and KMS for Dedicated/Private; hosted has managed keys with BYOK options for enterprise. we'll attach SOC2 docs.
[02:21] Priya: good. question on hosted: can you guarantee tail latency for streaming? we've seen other vendors with streaming hiccups when concurrency jumps.
[02:28] Jonah: streaming is more sensitive to small-queue delays; our runtime has continuous batching and KV cache to reduce per-token work. for short streaming flows we leverage prefix caching heavily; in many cases that drops p95 by 20-40% based on similarity to cached prefixes.
[02:45] Marcus: what's the expected tokens/sec per GPU for your 70B runner with quantization? numbers we've seen vary widely.
[02:51] Jonah: ballpark, depending on quant and attention kernels, a single A100-80GB-equivalent can do ~250-600 tokens/sec for short streaming under low concurrency if using int8 q8 setups; for 70B-family it can be lower. with batching and mixed-precision kernels throughput per GPU can increase but latency tradeoffs apply.
[03:10] Priya: that's a wide range. our traffic has many short 40-token responses, so tokens/sec matters but also per-token latency.
[03:18] Jonah: right. so for short chat flows we tune batch windows aggressively to keep latency under target — that reduces tokens/sec slightly but preserves p95. for sustained high concurrency bursts, Dedicated with reserved pools and autoscale burst capacity is usually better economically.
[03:34] Maya: to give a concrete scenario: if you need p95 server-side at 230ms for short flows and you have 300 steady concurrency, we can often serve that on Hosted with our default caching + small batch windows. if you hit 2.5k concurrency sustained, Hosted will route to larger clusters and costs go up; Dedicated with 4-6 reserved cards plus burst nodes would be more predictable.
[03:55] Samir: do you support colocated private deployments in our VPC?
[03:58] Jonah: yes, Redwood Private can be deployed inside your VPC/on-prem; that gives you full KMS/HSM and no egress. it does add ops lift and licensing.
[04:07] Priya: okay. let's talk numbers: what's the expected p95 delta between Hosted and Dedicated for streaming?
[04:12] Jonah: in our experience Hosted vs Dedicated p95 differences are usually under 10-15% for short flows if Hosted has capacity. The bigger differences show under noisy neighbor conditions or when you need guaranteed QoS during token storms — Dedicated gives consistent tail control via reserved queues and isolation.
[04:30] Marcus: curious about prefix/KV cache. if we have lots of repeated system prompts, how much tail improvement?
[04:35] Jonah: depends how much matches the cache. in internal evals we've seen 15-50% tail improvement when caching hits are frequent. but cache hit rate and keying are workload dependent.
[04:45] Priya: can you run a benchmark that simulates our burst profile?
[04:48] Maya: absolutely. here's the plan we're proposing: 1) you share traffic histogram 2) we build a harness that replays steady-state + spike bursts including streaming traces 3) run on Hosted and on a Dedicated-equivalent pool and measure server-side p95, p99, tokens/sec per GPU, and cost per million tokens.
[05:07] Samir: for the harness can you include network emulation to reflect our us-west latencies?
[05:11] Jonah: yes we can add a latency floor to the harness. we also include a prefix cache warm-up stage to measure warm and cold starts.
[05:18] Priya: timeline?
[05:20] Maya: we'll aim to deliver the harness plan by 2026-04-16 and run the first Hosted trial the week of 2026-04-20, pending traffic data.
[05:27] Priya: sounds good. pricing — can you ballpark Dedicated seat or reserved GPU cost vs Hosted for our expected pattern?
[05:33] Maya: we can provide sample math. Roughly, if you have frequent multi-minute bursts to 2.5k concurrency only very occasionally, Hosted with burst capacity is cheaper vs owning Dedicated. But if burst windows are common or sustained you may prefer reserved Dedicated for unit cost predictability. we'll send a model with expected monthly bill for your histogram.
[05:52] Marcus: how do rollouts work? can we pin model versions and fallback to smaller models if latency deteriorates?
[05:58] Jonah: yes, Redwood supports rollouts and automatic fallback policies — route to a lower-parameter model if latency/queueing crosses thresholds. also A/B canary for model updates.
[06:07] Priya: security checklist — we need SOC2 attestation, SAML SSO, per-route audit logs, long-term access logs for 1 year and KMS integration. Hosted can you offer those?
[06:17] Maya: hosted has SOC2 and audit logs; for SAML and one-year retention we offer enterprise add-on. KMS BYOK is available for Dedicated/Private, for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and managed keys or an enterprise BYOK option. we'll attach SOC2 and compliance docs.
[06:33] Samir: one more infra detail: we run some inference through an internal router; can Redwood's SDK handle per-request routing metadata and tracing headers?
[06:41] Jonah: yes, SDK supports request-level metadata, tracing hooks, and you can pass tenant headers for routing. we also expose token-level cost breakdowns in the console.
[06:49] Priya: benchmarks — what metrics should we expect in the report?
[06:52] Jonah: we'll include server-side p50/p95/p99 for latency, tokens/sec per instance, GPU utilization, batch sizes observed, cache hit rate, cost per million tokens, and recommended config (batch window, quantization profile, routing policy).
[07:08] Priya: perfect. any obvious red flags?
[07:11] Jonah: only one: if your burst 2.5k concurrency is both frequent and sustained, Hosted can become expensive and you may see tail increases unless you add reserved capacity. that's not a platform limitation, it's economics/runtime tradeoff.
[07:24] Maya: okay, recap: we will 1) send pricing and sample SLO math 2) Jonah will send the benchmark harness plan and scripts 3) Priya will share traffic histograms 4) schedule pilot the week of 4/20.
[07:36] Priya: agree. also can you include competitor comparisons for throughput? we looked at a few providers.
[07:41] Maya: sure, we'll include a short appendix comparing observed tokens/sec and tail behaviors against public numbers from Anthropic and HF where available.
[07:49] Marcus: quick question — cold start behavior for streaming: how do you mitigate first-request latency?
[07:54] Jonah: we use warm pools and pre-warmed KV caches for common prompts. we also offer small always-on footprint for latency-sensitive endpoints; that's a dedicated warm set.
[08:06] Priya: fine. last bit: can you demo a short streaming session with instrumentation in the pilot?
[08:10] Maya: yes, the pilot will include an observability session — token-level traces, per-route latency, and CDN/network overlays.
[08:18] Wrap / small crosstalk
[08:20] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll send the docs and proposed dates.
[08:23] Priya: thanks, appreciate it.
[08:24] Jonah: thanks all.

END
